solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: To fit into line's quite dodgy, with only one following

parts.note: just means quite, as in 'just right'

indicators.note: with only one says one of the doubled letters is dropped, leaving a single copy

parts.note: iffy means dodgy or doubtful
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone complains that squeezing text into a line is risky with only one character trailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with only one' keeps a single F (following) of the two in IFFY.
explanation.definitionFit: In typesetting, to justify text is to space it so each line fits the margins exactly.

clue.text: Picture breaking up

parts.note: a puzzle picture made of interlocking pieces is literally a picture broken up

explanation.surface: A television image dissolving into fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-up picture that is reassembled piece by piece is the familiar puzzle.

clue.text: Doubting Thomas infected, having caught cold

indicators.note: having caught means holding inside, as one catches a cold

parts.note: septic means infected
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: The apostle Thomas got an infection after catching a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having caught' puts C (cold) inside SEPTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubting Thomas, after the disciple who doubted the resurrection, is a person who doubts.

clue.text: Unseemly behaviour towards end of year over drink?

parts.note: in December is towards the end of the year, written IN DEC
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
rum is a drink

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour at a year-end party after too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towards end of year' gives IN DEC, in December.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is a lack of propriety, behaviour that breaks good manners.

clue.text: See attempt to get out at the Oval

definitions.meaning: a bishop's diocese, here an archbishop's

definitions.text: attempt to get out at the Oval
definitions.meaning: to bowl at a batsman with a yorker, a ball pitched at the feet

explanation.surface: A cricket fan is urged to watch a bowler try for a wicket at a London ground.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; a yorker is a delivery aimed at the batsman's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: The archbishopric is a see, and to york is cricket slang for bowling a yorker.

clue.text: Defender of faith originally to withdraw

parts.note: a back is a defender in football or rugby

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word faith

explanation.surface: The Defender of the Faith, a monarch's title, decides to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defender of faith' reads as the royal title, but it splits into a football defender, OF, and the first letter of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing off is a phrasal verb for retreating or stepping away from a position.

clue.text: Annoyed, as toast is unavailable

parts.note: toast is browned bread
off on a menu means no longer available

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated that their toast has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Browned off is British slang for fed up or irritated.

clue.text: Slightly raise bottom of fawn fabric

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom letter is the last, and raising it slightly moves it up one place

parts.note: to fawn is to creep or toady

explanation.surface: Lifting the hem of some fawn-coloured cloth a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slightly raise bottom of' moves the last letter of CREEP up one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a thin crinkled cloth, often silk.

clue.text: Unlikely faction blossoming at first

indicators.note: at first says the blooming piece comes before the faction

parts.note: flowers that are out are in bloom
a side is a faction or party

explanation.surface: An improbable political group flourishing early on.
explanation.definitionFit: An outside chance is a remote, improbable one.

clue.text: Pays for introducing unlimited extra measures

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something inside

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for it

indicators.note: unlimited means without its outer limits, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone pays to bring in additional measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'measures' looks like steps or policies, but here it means dances.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is a dance, and the foxtrot is a ballroom dance.

clue.text: Grouse shot circling bush, ornamental shrub

indicators.note: circling says the rearranged letters surround the bush
shot means wrecked or broken up, so the letters of grouse are rearranged

parts.note: the elder is a common bush

explanation.surface: A grouse is shot while flying round a bush in an ornamental garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' fits the gamebird surface but is the signal to rearrange its letters, which then go 'circling' the bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The guelder rose is a viburnum grown in gardens for its white snowball flowers.

clue.text: Are demanding courses for auditors

indicators.note: for auditors means for listeners, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: tacks are the courses a sailing boat steers into the wind

explanation.surface: Some degree courses are hard work for the people sitting in on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditors' suggests accountants, which fits the answer's sense too, but here they are simply hearers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that taxes you strains or makes heavy demands on you.

clue.text: Secure batting that bags a century

indicators.note: bags means captures or holds inside
batting means hitting about, so the letters of that are knocked into a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A batsman secures a hundred runs in a cricket innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batting' rearranges THAT to ATTH, and 'bags' puts A and C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something is to fasten or fix it, the same as joining it on.

clue.text: Suppose overthrow of French king is badly done?

parts.note: to infer is to conclude or suppose

indicators.note: overthrow turns the king upside down, so his name is read backwards

parts.note: roi is French for king

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether toppling a king of France was a poorly handled job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrow of' fits a deposed monarch, and here turns his French title back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior work is of low quality, poorly made; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Official introductory letter client read out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A formal letter of introduction is read aloud by a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read' looks like the action, but it is fodder alongside 'client'.
explanation.definitionFit: Credentials are papers giving proof of identity, such as an ambassador's letter.

clue.text: Caught gamebird leaving quiet region where slugs collected?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: leaving says the quiet letter goes out of the bird

parts.note: the partridge is a gamebird
P stands for piano, quiet in music
a belt is a region or zone, as in the corn belt

explanation.surface: A gamebird is caught and leaves a quiet area where garden slugs gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops P (quiet) from PARTRIDGE. Slugs are bullets, not garden pests.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolier-style belt holds ammunition, and slug is slang for a bullet.

clue.text: One record after another oddly omitted ruler's conclusions

indicators.note: after says the first record comes before the second

parts.note: another record, here an EP, an extended-play disc
I is the Roman numeral one
a log is a record, as kept on a ship

indicators.note: oddly omitted drops the odd-numbered letters and keeps the even ones

explanation.surface: A ruler's final words recorded one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' stands for a second record, an extended-play disc; 'oddly omitted' drops the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of the ruler's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Epilogues are closing passages, the conclusions of plays or books.

clue.text: 500 in complex image or Chinese character

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the rearranged letters
complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A complicated picture or a Chinese symbol, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges IMAGEOR, with D (500) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese writing uses ideograms, symbols standing for ideas.

clue.text: Drawing water from close current, eluding guards

indicators.note: guards means holds inside, protecting what it surrounds

parts.note: defying can mean resisting or eluding, as in defying description
close weather is humid
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: On a muggy day someone pulls water out of the air while dodging security guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' reads as security staff, but it is the verb, holding the close current inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dehumidifier removes moisture from the air, drawing water out of it.

clue.text: Who led row on failing to start dance?

indicators.note: failing to start says each word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A question about who headed the rowing crew in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to start' drops W, L, R and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk dance or party.

clue.text: Dog's last to find out about bitch

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the dog word

parts.note: to rumble someone is to find them out

explanation.surface: A dog is the last to learn about a female dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitch' looks like the female dog, but it is the verb to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To bitch is slang for to complain, and to grumble is to moan.

clue.text: Tight times just round the corner

parts.note: near means stingy, tight with money
by means times in multiplication, as in four by six

explanation.surface: Difficult times are just ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something round the corner is close at hand.

clue.text: Association gone from SW, presumably

parts.note: over means finished or gone
something moving away from the south-west is presumably heading to the north-east, written TO NE

explanation.surface: A society has left the south-west of England, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'gone from SW' suggests OVER TO NE: what has left the south-west has presumably gone over to the north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is a connotation or suggested association beyond a word's plain meaning.

clue.text: Lighter touch leads to easier relationships

parts.note: a tap is a light touch

indicators.note: leads to means the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gentler touch makes relationships easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' is a noun here, something that lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a thin candle or spill used to light fires.

clue.text: Publication that listeners may turn down

definitions.meaning: a single book or a numbered issue in a series
loudness of a radio, which those hearing it may lower

explanation.surface: A book that readers might reject, cast in terms of a radio audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume is one book, and volume is also the loudness turned down on a dial.

clue.text: Audibly challenged foreign agent casing area to north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going to north means reading upwards
casing means wrapping in a case, so the agent surrounds the area letter

parts.note: a fed is an American federal agent

explanation.surface: A hard-of-hearing foreign spy staking out a northern area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casing' puts A inside FED to make FAED; 'to north' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to hear is being hard of hearing, the plain meaning.

clue.text: Greek character from western half of island

indicators.note: in an across clue the western half is the left half, the first three letters

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A Greek person from the west of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western half of' keeps the left three letters of RHODES.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Maybe two or three more dead following charge

indicators.note: following says the dead piece comes after the charge

parts.note: to prime a gun is to charge it with powder
number read as numb-er means more numb, more dead to feeling

explanation.surface: Two or three more people killed after a cavalry charge, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more dead' reads NUMBER as numb plus -er, more lacking sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Two and three are examples of integers divisible only by one and themselves.

clue.text: Some among relatives of mixed blood

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Several family members have mixed ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel is a dog of mixed breed, so of mixed parentage.

clue.text: Traditional industry the queen's invested in arousing suspicion

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, as money is put into a business

parts.note: fishy means suspicious or questionable
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen; the 's is just 'is', joining the pieces

explanation.surface: The monarch has put money into something that looks dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' reads as putting money into a venture; here it puts the queen inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing grounds and the business of catching fish are an age-old trade.
